message.content:
Below is a list of the **long weekends** that occurred in Canada during 2023.  
A long weekend is defined as a holiday that falls on a Friday or a Monday, creating a three‑day weekend (Friday–Saturday–Sunday or Friday–Saturday–Sunday).  

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Day of Week | Long Weekend (Date Range) |
|---------|-------------|-------------|---------------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 | Sunday | Jan 1–2 (Sunday–Monday) |
| Family Day (Ontario, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Saskatchewan) | Feb 20 | Monday | Feb 18–20 (Friday–Sunday) |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 | Friday | Apr 7–9 (Friday–Sunday) |
| Victoria Day | May 22 | Monday | May 20–22 (Friday–Sunday) |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 | Saturday | Jul 1–2 (Saturday–Sunday) |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 | Monday | Sep 2–4 (Friday–Sunday) |
| Thanksgiving | Oct 9 | Monday | Oct 7–9 (Friday–Sunday) |
| Remembrance Day | Nov 11 | Monday | Nov 9–11 (Friday–Sunday) |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 | Monday | Dec 23–25 (Friday–Sunday) |

**Notes**

1. **Family Day** is observed in several provinces (Ontario, Manitoba, New Brunswick, Saskatchewan). Other provinces have different holidays on that week (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador, Louis Riel Day in Manitoba, etc.).  
2. **Boxing Day** (Dec 26) is a holiday in some provinces but does not create a long weekend in 2023 because it falls on a Tuesday.  
3. Some provinces have additional holidays that create long weekends (e.g., St. Patrick’s Day in Newfoundland & Labrador on March 17, 2023). If you need province‑specific long weekends, let me know!
